findings.text: non-blocking: the `_RUNNER_FAILURE_SUMMARY` branch can never change a verdict. Admission past promotion_checks.py:2157 (`elif not control_ids`) requires a non-empty `control_ids`, which is the same `review_module.gate_log_failure_ids` call the preceding line already returned truthy for, so `_runner_reports_a_failed_run` returns True at line 1080 and the `N failed` summary regex is never what admits a log. Both this function's docstring and the dispatch prompt in reckon/crew/prompts.py:311 name the summary as a second record that decides, and no test passes a summary-only log, so a regression in the regex would go unnoticed.

non-blocking: the arm pair is not one population. `after_suite` cites gate.log for the single new test file while `baseline_suite` cites gate-base.log for the four importer files, so the two fields do not measure the same suite at base and head; the head arm that does cover the importer population is gate-head.log (20 passed), recorded only under test_logs and artifacts, and its own header line 1 names revision 7f41f27119 with an uncommitted working tree rather than head 0da707fa24. A reader taking the suite fields as a base/head pair reads two different suites as one.

non-blocking: three changed paths lie outside the dispatch's exclusive write scope — this file, tests/test_control_is_compared_with_the_head_arm.py and reckon/crew/prompts.py — and only the last is named by the plan's own write-paths clause. The two legacy test edits are required: each asserted the retired refusal and would fail at head without the update. The worker disclosed all three under outside_scope and blockers, and the self-widen was refused by a read-only crew lock directory, so the coordinator must widen the three paths before promotion.

non-blocking: `assert _control_run_shows_a_failure(f"...EXIT=1\n", 1) is True` passes the same fact twice — the status is handed to the function as an argument and restates what the log text already says — and it still passes under the declared mutation, so it survives the regression the test exists to catch. Line 138 carries this test's durability; line 139 only re-asserts that `recorded != 0`.

justifications.durability: Removing the runner-record branch reddens exactly the three cases it protects — promotion_evidence.py:1080's guard, the runner-red admission at tests/test_a_negative_control_is_read_from_the_runner.py:91 and the head-arm refusal at :116 — but the `N failed` summary branch at promotion_evidence.py:1082 has no test that can redden on it.
justifications.evidence: gate.log records 5 passed EXIT=0 and negative-control.log records 3 failed 2 passed EXIT=1, but the manifest's after_suite cites gate.log for one file against a baseline_suite of four files, and the two legacy test edits have no named log at all.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1085 sits beside `_recorded_exit_status` at :1044 and follows the module's mechanism-comment idiom, with no plan, sprint or ticket label in any added symbol or docstring.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2148 replaces the EXIT-gated refusal with `_control_run_shows_a_failure`, so a runner-written red log with FAILED ids and no capture line is admitted while the id-identity and arm-comparison refusals are untouched.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1080 routes the failure decision through `review_module.gate_log_failure_ids`, the repository's single format-aware log reader, and extends `_require_declared_negative_control` rather than forking a second control gate; only the `_RUNNER_FAILURE_SUMMARY` regex at :1017 restates a shape `_RUNNER_SUMMARY` at :1009 already matches.
justifications.scope_discipline: reckon/crew/prompts.py:302, tests/test_control_gate_checks_facts.py:144 and tests/test_control_is_compared_with_the_head_arm.py:229 all changed outside the dispatch's declared write paths, disclosed but not widened.

verdicts.call_sites: reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2452 calls _require_declared_negative_control, which reaches the new reader at :2148; reckon/crew/promotion.py:2390 imports the check into the promotion path; reckon/crew/prompts.py:369 and :806 carry the contract sentence into every composed implement prompt.
verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit over 7f41f27119..0da707fa24: 8901431b8a carries the reader, the gate, the prompt contract and the three test edits, 0da707fa24 adds only the 77-line evidence fragment; nothing in either commit is unrelated to §2.
verdicts.done_when: The done_when names tests/test_a_negative_control_is_read_from_the_runner.py; gate.log records 5 passed EXIT=0 at head 0da707fa24, and the importer clause is covered by gate-head.log 20 passed against gate-base.log 15 passed, 0 added failures.
verdicts.goal: The node's goal is to admit a negative control on the runner's own record; reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2148 now takes the failure from `_control_run_shows_a_failure` instead of requiring a terminal EXIT line, and the four cases §2 names — runner-written red log admitted, bare EXIT=1 refused, id the head arm also fails refused, composed prompt naming the contract — are each asserted and green.
verdicts.manifest: Read; it states status complete, names its four gate logs, records baseline_suite and after_suite as completed with zero failures, and its own rubric self-checks are filled — but its suite fields pair two different populations (finding at manifest.md:18).
verdicts.write_paths: The manifest's declared paths list promotion_checks.py, promotion_evidence.py, the new test and the evidence fragment; the diff also carries reckon/crew/prompts.py, tests/test_control_gate_checks_facts.py and tests/test_control_is_compared_with_the_head_arm.py, all three outside that list and disclosed under outside_scope.
